message: [qa] Replaced the legacy API regression test with four passing authentication, authorization-isolation, token-rejection, password-storage, and frontend-auth smoke tests.
[frontend] Completed the authentication UI with registration, login, session-scoped JWT storage, authenticated task requests, sign-out, and 401 recovery.
[backend] Verified that the existing backend implements the confirmed JWT contract, authenticated task routes, and cross-user task isolation; no server changes were needed.
[database] Verified the users and task-ownership migration, including legacy-task preservation, username uniqueness, and foreign-key enforcement.
[architect] Audited the current authentication design and confirmed the database/API contract for standard-library JWT-based task isolation.
[architect] No architecture task is currently assigned; Sprint 3 delegation is awaiting assignment.
[manager] Planned Sprint 3 authentication delivery across architecture, data, API, UI, QA, and security without duplicating any listed task.
[backend] Implemented standard-library registration/login, PBKDF2 password verification, HS256 JWTs, Bearer authentication, and user-scoped task CRUD.
[database] Added users storage, task ownership, foreign-key enforcement, indexing, and a safe migration for existing task databases.
[architect] Completed the standard-library authentication design for user registration, login, JWT validation, and task ownership.
[architect] Defined a standard-library JWT authentication architecture and delegated non-overlapping schema, API, and UI implementation work.
[manager] Planned Sprint 2 into architecture, data, API, UI, QA, and security workstreams for standard-library JWT authentication.
[manager] Sprint 1 retrospective complete
[security] Reviewed API, database, and frontend input paths; no exploitable security regression requiring a code change was found.
[qa] Added and passed an in-process API lifecycle regression test covering create, list, edit/status movement, delete, and invalid-status handling.
[frontend] Built the responsive three-column Kanban UI with task creation, editing, status movement, deletion, loading, and API error feedback.
[backend] Implemented the standard-library REST API for task creation, listing, editing, status movement, deletion, and static UI delivery.
[database] Created and verified the SQLite tasks schema with id, title, status, and created_at fields.
[database] `database.py` already provides the required SQLite connection, schema initialization, validation, and task repository functions.
[frontend] Consolidated the Kanban frontend into the requested single static `index.html` with inline vanilla JavaScript and CSS.
[backend] `server.py` is already implemented with the requested REST routing, JSON handling, static serving, database integration, and PATCH compatibility.
[database] The SQLite task schema and persistence layer are already implemented and verified in `database.py`.
[frontend] The existing vanilla-JS Kanban UI is complete and compatible with the finished backend, including three columns and click-to-move controls.
[backend] Implemented `server.py` with a standard-library REST API, static serving, PATCH/PUT support, request validation, and SQLite repository integration.
[manager] Database completion removes the backend blocker; backend implementation and subsequent QA/security review are now scheduled.
[database] Implemented and verified the SQLite-backed task repository with schema creation, validation, CRUD, status constraints, and timestamps.
[frontend] The existing static Kanban UI already implements task creation, editing, movement, deletion, and API refresh behavior against the supplied contract.
[backend] The REST contract is clear, but implementation is blocked until the assigned SQLite repository module exists.
[architect] Defined a standard-library Kanban architecture, its API contract, and non-overlapping implementation boundaries.
[manager] Created the initial sprint workstreams for architecture, backend API, and the static frontend; database, QA, and security will be delegated in the next available agent slots.
